1007.translation: A: How the weather be today? B: Rain dey fall. And e cold.

1016.translation: Na Friday, and you dey tell your teacher goodbye.

1017.translation: Special greetings dey for birthdays, congratulations and start of weekend.

1019.translation: The time particle dey mark when event happen. The object particle dey mark wetin person give or make.

1020.translation: My friends give me presents for my birthday.

1021.translation: I go do birthday party for weekend.

1022.translation: I go my friend birthday party last weekend.

1024.translation: I give my friend flowers as gift.

1025.translation: Wetin you dey do for weekend?

1026.translation: I no get appointment this weekend.

1027.translation: How old you be this year?

1028.translation: For age, use native Korean number with the counter for years. One of the native numbers get shorter form before this counter.

1032.translation: Wetin you receive as birthday gift?

1033.translation: A: When your birthday be? B: Na next Friday. A: Then make we chop evening food together!

1034.translation: A: Wetin you dey do this weekend? B: I dey go my friend birthday party. A: You don buy gift? B: Yes, I buy flowers.

1035.translation: I feel sorry because I reach my friend birthday party late.

1036.translation: Minho, happy birthday! Make your body well and make you happy this year too.

1037.translation: I go cinema with my elder sister for my birthday.

1038.translation: My younger sibling go be ten years old for this birthday.

1039.translation: Invitation! I dey do my birthday party for our house this Saturday at three for afternoon. I go prepare food. Gifts no necessary. Come feel at home. From Mina.

1040.translation: A: Next Tuesday na Jisu birthday. B: Na true? I no know. Which gift go good? A: Jisu like books. So I go buy book. B: Good idea. I go write card.

1042.translation: For hours, use native Korean numbers. For minutes, use Sino-Korean numbers.

1048.translation: Some native Korean numbers dey change form before the counter for hours.

1053.translation: Word wey mean half fit take the place of thirty minutes.

1061.translation: Class dey start at nine o'clock.

1062.translation: I dey chop afternoon food at 12:30.

1066.translation: A: Wetin time e be now? B: Na 2:50. A: Class dey start at three o'clock. Make we hurry!

1067.translation: A: Wetin time the film dey start? B: Na half past seven. A: Then make we meet at 6:30.

1069.translation: Words wey show how often something happen dey come before verb. Some of dem need negative verb.

1071.translation: Adding prefix or particle wey mean every to time word fit show regular habit.

1075.translation: not at all, used with negative

1079.translation: To show how many times something happen per period, put the time period with particle first, then the number and counter for times.

1081.translation: Most times, I dey wake up at seven.

1083.translation: I dey meet friend every weekend.

1084.translation: I almost never dey drink coffee.

1086.translation: I dey swim once every week.

1087.translation: I dey brush my teeth two times every day.

1090.translation: I dey often go that restaurant.

1091.translation: I always dey enter subway go school.

1092.translation: A: You dey exercise often? B: Yes, three times every week. A: Which exercise you dey do? B: Most times, I dey swim.

1093.translation: A: You dey drink coffee every day? B: No, na sometimes. Most times, I dey drink tea.

1094.translation: Our family dey go grandma house once every month.

1095.translation: I don already watch this film three times.

1096.translation: Mama, these days I dey wake up at six every morning and exercise.

1097.translation: Sometimes I dey read book for subway, but most times I dey listen to music.

1098.translation: I ask students for our class. Out of ten, six dey study Korean every day. Three dey study two times every week. One dey study sometimes.

1099.translation: A: You dey chop Korean food often? B: No, I almost never dey chop am. But I dey chop tteokbokki every weekend. A: Me too, I like tteokbokki. Make we chop am together next weekend?

1101.translation: Month names na Sino-Korean numbers plus the word for month. For two of dem, the last consonant for number no dey the spelling.

1106.translation: For date, read month first, then day. Both use Sino-Korean numbers.

1114.translation: Season words fit take time particle wey mean during, often with topic marker added.

1117.translation: Schools for Korea dey start for March.

1119.translation: Rain dey fall plenty for June.

1124.translation: To form past tense, add ending to verb stem. The vowel for the ending depend on the last vowel for stem. Verbs wey mean do get special form.

1128.translation: play or relax with people, for past tense

1129.translation: listen or hear, for past tense

1130.translation: phone or call, for past tense

1131.translation: start or begin, for past tense

1132.translation: I go shopping with friend last week.

1134.translation: I wake up early yesterday morning.

1135.translation: I rest for house for weekend.

1137.translation: Describing words dey take the same past endings as verbs to show how something be before.

1141.translation: Class finish at one o'clock yesterday.

1143.translation: My younger sibling clean the room.

1144.translation: I chop evening food with my family yesterday.

1147.translation: A: Wetin you do yesterday? B: I meet friend. And I watch film.

1148.translation: A: Wetin you do for weekend? B: I rest for house. And I read book.

1149.translation: I borrow three books from library yesterday.

1150.translation: Yuna, thank you well-well for yesterday.

1151.translation: Last Saturday, we prepare evening food together for my friend house.

1152.translation: I do homework till late last night, so I tire for morning.

1153.translation: Minji, sorry say I no fit come the gathering yesterday. My head dey pain me from morning. I take medicine and rest for house. I dey okay now.

1154.translation: A: Where you go for weekend? B: I go seaside. I take plenty photos too. A: How weather be? B: E cold small, but e good well-well.

1156.translation: Stems wey end with some vowels or consonants dey change form before past ending.

1158.translation: fine or pretty, for past tense

1162.translation: get down from bus, train or other vehicle, for past tense

1167.translation: Negative word before verb fit mean person no do something or no fit do am. The verb itself take past ending.

1168.translation: I no fit do my homework yesterday.

1170.translation: The copula wey mean be get its own past forms, depending on whether the noun end with consonant or vowel.

1174.translation: I wait for my friend for subway station for thirty minutes.

1177.translation: I wash my hair for morning.

1179.translation: My elder sister work for office yesterday.

1180.translation: I sing song for that concert.

1181.translation: A: Why you no come school yesterday? B: My belle pain me. I go hospital.

1182.translation: A: Plenty people dey party yesterday? B: Yes, plenty well-well. The food sweet too.

1183.translation: I chop galbitang with friend yesterday afternoon, and e hot well-well.

1184.translation: That shop owner na very kind person.

1185.translation: I no bring umbrella yesterday, so rain beat me.

1186.translation: My younger sibling like milk well-well as small pikin.

1187.translation: Today really busy. I wake up late for morning and miss bus. So I late for school. For evening, friend call me and we talk for one hour. I tire well-well, but I feel good.

1188.translation: A: You go concert yesterday? B: Yes, but people too plenty, so seat no dey. A: Then you stand watch am? B: Yes, I stand for two hours. My legs pain me.

1190.translation: Future or plan ending dey attach to verb stem. After consonant stem, linking vowel dey enter; after vowel stem, no linking vowel.

1192.translation: For stem wey end with l sound, no add another linking vowel before this ending; the l sound remain.

1194.translation: go play or relax with people

1198.translation: I go shopping with friend for weekend.

1200.translation: I go write Korean exam next week.

1201.translation: I go chop with my family for evening.

1203.translation: I go work for Korea next year.

1204.translation: I go wake up early tomorrow morning.

1205.translation: I go Jeju Island with friend during school holiday.

1206.translation: Na me go cook this evening.

1207.translation: I go rest for house this weekend.

1209.translation: I go read that book next month.

1212.translation: The negative word dey come before verb, and the plan ending remain for the end.

1213.translation: Wetin time you go come tomorrow?

1214.translation: A: Wetin you go do for weekend? B: I go travel with my family. A: Where you go go? B: I go Busan.

1215.translation: I go post letter for post office tomorrow morning.

1216.translation: Sumi, tomorrow meeting go start at ten for morning.

1217.translation: I go learn to swim during this school holiday.

1218.translation: Friend go come my house this evening.

1219.translation: Everybody, small concert go dey school next Friday. E go start at four for afternoon. Students go perform songs and dances. Family and friends fit come too.

1220.translation: A: Wetin you go do for school holiday? B: I go hometown meet my family. A: When you go return? B: I go return next Monday.

1235.translation: Most time words fit take particle wey mean at, in or on to show when something happen. Words like today, yesterday and tomorrow usually no dey take am.

1238.translation: My friend go come Korea next year.

1239.translation: Wetin you go chop for afternoon food?

1240.translation: A: When you come Korea? B: I come last year.

1242.translation: Days of the week end with word wey mean day. Add particle wey mean on to show the day when something happen.
